thread:
Ava Kim: quick idea — we should add a "bill of token components" panel to the cost dashboard. show per-request line items: model_compute, kv_cache_credit, routing_surcharge, postprocess_tokens. short, sortable rows.
Rohit Patel: +1. also need clear allocation rules when multiple routes share the same cached model instance. propose we split cache savings by route traffic share during the window.
Dana Li: splitting by traffic share is noisy. routes that cause warmups (heavy first requests) should get a larger portion of the credit. suggest: first-writer gets warmup credit for N minutes, remaining hits amortized.
Maya Gonzales: UX note — expose a toggle: attribution mode = [by_request | by_owner | hybrid(warmup-first)]. show both absolute $ and % of route bill. customers asked for per-model unit economics (cost per successful response, cost per 1k completions).
Victor L.: how do we compute "cache savings" precisely? baseline matters. simplest formula: savings = cost_no_cache - cost_with_cache. but cost_no_cache needs a simulated/inferred token path or a historical baseline.
ops-bot: billing snapshot: model-x KV-cache reduced token compute by 11.7% last 24h across all routes (:chart_with_downwards_trend:). link: https://console.redwood/billing/snapshots/2026-06-18
Rohit Patel: SQL sketch to allocate cache credit (very rough):
```sql
WITH hits AS (
  SELECT route, request_id, is_cache_hit FROM requests WHERE ts BETWEEN $start AND $end
), owner_share AS (
  SELECT route, COUNT(*)::float / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS share FROM hits GROUP BY route
)
SELECT o.route, total_savings * o.share AS allocated_credit
FROM owner_share o CROSS JOIN (SELECT SUM(sim_cost - actual_cost) AS total_savings FROM requests WHERE ts BETWEEN $start AND $end) s;
```
Dana Li: small concern: that cross-join approach loses the warmup writer logic. need an extra CTE to identify warmup windows and assign them priority.
Maya Gonzales: product ask — add a "preview charge" mode for dev teams so they can see expected monthly impact before enabling caching/quantization. keep it off by default.
Ava Kim: fallback question — when we rollout a model variant, should historical cache credits stay with the old model version or migrate? my vote: credits are tied to model_version at request time; rollups can show an aggregated switch-over view.
Victor L.: edge case: deduping repeated conversational responses (retries/concurrent requests) — we might double-credit cache savings. rule: only first serviced request in a dedupe window is eligible for warmup credit.
Rohit Patel: I'll add a more complete allocation query and a short perf sim this week. can someone mock the UI rows? I can wire the backfill metrics.
Ava Kim: I'll prototype a panel with columns: route, owner_team, model_version, requests, cache_hits, cache_savings($), compute_cost($), net_cost($), allocation_rule. will push a PR to infra/dashboards.
